prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universal “best” broker — the right one depends on your budget, medical needs, whether you want Marketplace (ACA) coverage or off‑exchange options, and how much hand‑holding you want. Instead of a single name, here’s a practical way to find the best health insurance broker in Kansas City, MO for a self‑employed person, plus tools and the questions to ask.

What to look for in a broker
- Independent (not captive to one carrier) so they can shop multiple insurers.  
- Marketplace‑certified (if you want ACA/subsidy help).  
- Experience with self‑employed clients and with subsidies, Form 1095‑A, and SEP/Schedule C implications.  
- Transparent about fees (many are paid by carriers but some charge consulting fees).  
- Good reviews and quick, clear communication.  
- Will show you total cost (premiums + deductible/out‑of‑pocket + network/co‑pays) and explain provider networks.  

Where to find reputable brokers/agents
- NAHU (National Association of Health Underwriters) “Find an Agent” tool.  
- Independent Insurance Agents & Brokers of America (Big I) directory.  
- Kansas Insurance Department license lookup to verify an agent’s license/status.  
- Local Google/Yelp reviews and BBB ratings for Kansas City agents.  
- Online marketplaces for quotes and brokers: HealthSherpa (good for ACA enrollment), eHealth (comparisons + brokers).  

Questions to ask any broker before you hire them
- Are you independent or do you represent specific carriers? Which ones?  
- Are you certified to enroll people through the ACA Marketplace?  
- Do you charge any fees? If so, how much and when?  
- How many self‑employed/1099 clients have you helped? Can you provide references?  
- Will you compare on‑ and off‑exchange plans and explain subsidy eligibility?  
- How quickly will you provide quotes and application help? Do you help with renewals/claims?  
- How do you help with provider/network checks and prescription drug coverage?  

Types of brokers/places to consider
- Local independent agents who work with multiple carriers — best if you want personal service and local market knowledge.  
- Online brokerages (HealthSherpa, eHealth) — good for fast comparisons and ACA enrollment, sometimes less personalized.  
- Direct carrier agents (e.g., Blue Cross Blue Shield of Kansas City) — good if you prefer one carrier but less choice.

Next step I can do for you
- If you give me your ZIP code and whether you need family coverage, whether you want ACA marketplace plans (subsidies), or if you’re looking for high‑deductible/HSA plans or short‑term coverage, I can find and list 3–5 well‑rated local independent brokers and provide contact links and recent reviews.
